item.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects second contract offer
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected the club’s second offer to extend his contract, leaving negotiations over the Portugal midfielder’s future unresolved. BBC Sport reports that Fernandes is out of contract at the end of the season, although United can extend his deal by 12 months, until 2028. The club wants to agree a new contract before using that option. If no agreement is reached, United are expected to trigger the extension before January 1. Without it, Fernandes would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from that date, with six months remaining on his deal. It is unclear when Fernandes rejected the offer. A resolution does not appear imminent amid the upheaval at Old Trafford: Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as head coach. United will hope Pochettino’s arrival can persuade Fernandes to stay. The midfielder came close to joining Pochettino’s Tottenham in 2019, before moving from Sporting to United six months later. He has scored six goals in 13 appearances for United this season. BBC chief football news reporter Simon Stone says Fernandes wants to compete for the biggest prizes and will want to see what impact Pochettino has at United. The club, meanwhile, must weigh the cost and length of a new deal against Fernandes’ recent drop in form after an outstanding previous season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won major player-of-the-year awards. Fernandes is 32, and a new contract could commit United to a substantial outlay over several years. Both sides may therefore have reasons to take their time, despite the club’s wish to keep its captain. Arthur’s birth extended a family tradition that began with his great-great-grandfather, Wilber Harlow, who was born on September 14, 1907. The other family members who share the birthday are Wilber’s daughter, Addie Harlow, born on September 14, 1949; his grandson, Donald Harlow, born on September 14, 1972; and his great-granddaughter, Emma Bell, born on September 14, 1997. Emma is Arthur’s mother, while Donald is his grandfather. item.title: U-23 AFCONQ: Nigeria suffer 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in first leg
item.description: Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0 to DR Congo in the first leg of their second-round qualifying tie. The Nigerian side, led by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Osehai Ozebagbe and former Nigeria U-20 assistant coach Deniran Ortega, struggled to convert their early opportunities as the hosts secured a comfortable advantage ahead of the return fixture. The coaching duo took charge in the absence of Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle, who was occupied with Nigeria’s senior national team preparations for their crucial Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. Nigeria started brightly and nearly took the lead in the fourth minute when Victor Samuel’s effort missed the target. The midfielder had another opportunity five minutes later after finding himself one-on-one with the DR Congo goalkeeper but failed to convert. The missed chances proved costly as DR Congo took the lead in the 20th minute in controversial circumstances. Nigeria goalkeeper Samuel James appeared to have been fouled by a Congolese player while attempting to collect an aerial ball during the build-up to the opening goal. However, the referee allowed the goal to stand. The Olympic Eagles suffered another setback in the 30th minute when Brighton youngster Zadok Yohanna was forced off with an injury. DR Congo doubled their advantage five minutes before the break through Felozefe Mabete, who produced an impressive free-kick to put the hosts firmly in control. Despite their attempts to find a way back into the contest after the restart, Nigeria could not break down the Congolese defence, with the hosts protecting their two-goal advantage until the final whistle. The result leaves the Olympic Eagles with a difficult task in the second leg, as they must overturn the deficit to keep their qualification hopes alive. Nigeria will host DR Congo in the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, where they will seek to secure an aggregate victory and advance to the final qualifying round. The Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations also serves as the qualification pathway for the men’s football tournament at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. item.title: Boko Haram: Zulum announces ₦50k for each soldier deployed to Borno communities
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities of Maiwa and Koshebe villages. Our Correspondent report that Koshebe in November 28, 2020 came under massacre when some armed Boko Haram militants launched a devastating attack on peasant and laborer rice farmers working in the fields (near Zabarmari and Maiduguri), where over 100 farm laborers—many of whom traveled from Sokoto State in northwest Nigeria for seasonal harvest work—were rounded up, tied, and their throats slit. Likewise, in November, 2023, suspected Boko Haram insurgents again targeted rice farmers harvesting crops in the Karkut and Koshebe general areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 farmers and leaving others missing. But Zulum assured that he will provide the needed support to strengthen security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, ensure safe travel, and revive trade in communities recovering from years of insurgency. The Governor gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. The highway links communities along the corridor to markets and facilitates the movement of agricultural produce, essential commodities and other goods. Zulum said improving security along the route would help residents travel safely, trade and rebuild their livelihoods. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe villages, the governor pledged “to provide operational logistics and sustain welfare support. He announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities”. Governor Zulum’s administration has consistently supported military operations with logistics and welfare assistance as part of efforts to improve security and help displaced residents return to their communities. The Governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. item.title: Conversion to university: We are waiting for release of government gazette – Abdul, YABATECH Rector
item.description: By Adesina Wahab The conversion of Yaba College of Technology, YABATECH, to the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies is being delayed because the Federal Government is yet to release the official gazette that would convey that, the Rector, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, has disclosed. He stated this on Friday while answering questions on the sideline of the press briefing to herald the 38th convocation ceremonies of the College. “We are pretty much on course to becoming a University. The bill has been passed by the National Assembly and it has been signed into law by President Bola Tinubu. At our end, we are adequately prepared. What remains now is for the official gazette to be released by the Federal Government. When that is done, the institutional evaluation will be conducted by the Federal Ministry of Education and then the National Universities Commission, NUC, would come and accredit our courses. “Indeed, this historic conversion reflects the growing recognition by the President and the larger society of the importance of technology-driven and Vocational education in addressing Nigeria’s human-capital and industrial development needs,” he said. As part of the convocation ceremonies, Dr Abdul said the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, the Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele and Mrs Itunu Omotayo would be conferred Fellowship of the College. Also, Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, will deliver the convocation lecture titled ” From silos to synergy: Reimagining Nigeria’s tertiary education system for national transformation”. The event will be chaired by the Minister of State for Education, Prof.Suwaiba Ahmad. Giving a breakdown of the number of graduating students, the Rector said a total of 10,886 would be involved. Out of the figure, 361 are graduating with distinction, 3,160 earned upper credit pass, 5,696 are graduating with lower credit pass and 1,669 have pass grade. Abdul added that the College has continued to promote entrepreneurship as an essential component of its education philosophy and that the citing of the Folawiyo Entrepreneurship Centre in the College was a testament to that . item.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
item.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. item.content:encoded: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. item.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. item.title: Jaji wins Zamfara APC rerun primary with 26,646 votes
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. item.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
item.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. item.title: 10 footballers with the most red cards in football history
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Footballers are often praised for keeping their cool when the stakes are high, but some of the game’s most recognisable names have become known for receiving repeated red cards. From tough-tackling defenders to forceful midfielders, their careers have combined success on the pitch with frequent disciplinary woes. Gerardo Bedoya stands clear at the top of the ranking, with 46 red cards during his playing career and recognised by the Guinness World Records. The former Colombia international’s fiery reputation followed him into coaching: in 2016, he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as an assistant coach at Santa Fe. Red-card totals can differ between databases because no single global record tracks every player’s dismissals across all competitions. The NIS, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) and other stakeholders convened at a sensitisation workshop at the NIS headquarters on Friday in Abuja. The workshop is themed: “The Role of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Election Monitoring and Management.” Speaking at the workshop, the NIS Comptroller-General, Mrs Kemi Nandap, said that the successful conduct of the upcoming elections required institutional cooperation from all security stakeholders. item.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
item.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. item.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
item.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Photo of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the federal government delegation in Abuja, on Thursday. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. The Federal Government said the agreement was part of its broader efforts to attract private-sector investment and expertise into the development and management of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure. Under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development has pursued reforms aimed at modernising airports, improving operational efficiency and strengthening the aviation sector’s contribution to economic growth. The Port Harcourt airport concession is expected to improve the passenger experience, strengthen airport services, and attract investment to the facility. item.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. item.title: Is Galadima the Round Peg in the Round Hole for Adamawa?

Situated in Nigeria’s North-East, the state has long balanced agricultural potential with security challenges, urban expansion with rural neglect, and a politically vibrant electorate with shifting party loyalties. For a party seeking to reclaim power in Adamawa from the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, unity is more than desirable; it is essential. Galadima’s ability to attract support across competing blocs suggests he enjoys both political goodwill and strategic alliances. Yet politics in Adamawa extends beyond party arithmetic. The electorate remains deeply concerned about security, particularly in communities affected by the spillover of insurgency in the North-East. Farmers want safer farmlands, traders need secure transport corridors, and young people seek economic opportunities that do not require leaving the state. Any candidate seeking to be regarded as the “right fit” must present credible solutions to these interconnected challenges. Supporters argue that Galadima’s administrative experience positions him to drive economic renewal. Adamawa’s economy remains largely agrarian, with significant untapped potential in agro-processing, livestock production and cross-border trade with neighbouring Cameroon. With improved infrastructure, targeted investment incentives and better access to rural finance, the state could move beyond subsistence agriculture towards value-added production. His backers contend that his experience at the federal level provides both the managerial expertise and institutional networks needed to facilitate that transition. Critics, however, caution that technocratic credentials do not automatically translate into political effectiveness. Governing Adamawa requires navigating ethnic diversity, balancing the interests of the three senatorial districts, and maintaining delicate relationships among traditional rulers, religious leaders and political stakeholders. A successful governor must be as comfortable engaging local communities as participating in policy discussions. For Galadima, the real test will be not only competence but connection. Another dimension of the debate concerns generational expectations. Adamawa has a large, youthful and increasingly digitally connected population. Social media now shapes political narratives as much as traditional campaigns, amplifying both achievements and shortcomings. For many younger voters, the “right fit” is measured less by seniority than by responsiveness, transparency, job creation and inclusive governance. Galadima’s campaign will need to engage directly with these expectations if it hopes to inspire support beyond the party faithful. There is also the broader question of continuity versus change. Some voters favour stability, arguing that governance should not shift dramatically with every electoral cycle. Others believe the state requires a decisive departure from established patterns. Galadima must therefore strike a delicate balance—projecting continuity where it inspires confidence while offering enough innovation to convince reform-minded voters that meaningful change is possible. Within the APC’s internal calculations, he may well be the ideal candidate. The party appears more united than in previous election cycles, and early reconciliation efforts suggest it has learned from the divisions that undermined its past electoral fortunes. Winning Adamawa, however, will require more than party cohesion. It demands an organisation capable of mobilising effectively across all 21 local government areas. In that respect, Galadima’s emergence has reduced internal friction and given the party a clearer direction. Statewide acceptability, however, is a different proposition. Adamawa’s political culture rewards accessibility. Elections are not won solely on policy documents or campaign promises but through consistent engagement with communities—condolence visits, town hall meetings and personal interactions that reinforce public trust. The months ahead will determine whether Galadima can translate elite endorsements into genuine grassroots momentum. Ultimately, describing Galadima as “the round peg in the round hole” may be premature. The phrase suggests inevitability—a seamless alignment between candidate and circumstance. Politics, particularly in Adamawa, is rarely that straightforward. It is fluid, shaped by evolving alliances, economic realities and changing voter sentiment. What can be said with confidence is that Galadima enters the race with notable strengths: administrative experience, broad intra-party support and a reputation for competence. Whether those qualities resonate beyond party delegates and political insiders will determine whether he emerges not only as the APC’s preferred candidate but also as Adamawa’s preferred choice. As 2027 approaches, the electorate will judge more than campaign rhetoric. Voters will examine records, scrutinise promises and assess authenticity. If Galadima can present a convincing vision for security, economic growth and inclusive governance—while demonstrating the accessibility and humility that Adamawa’s voters value—he may indeed prove to be the right fit for the state’s aspirations. Until then, the phrase remains both a compliment and a question—an assertion awaiting the verdict of the electorate. Habila Musa-Luka is a business executive based in Lagos, Nigeria.
